title: Project-owner context: ERP selection
claims: The project owner reports that Savvy uses Campfire ERP.
The relationship, modules, tenant configuration, and API access were not publicly or privately verified.

title: Independent RIA platform for financial advisors
claims: Savvy describes a proprietary platform combined with billing, compliance, custodial and operational services.
Advisor payout economics are described by book; no universal share percentage is established.

title: Solutions for independent financial advisors
claims: Savvy describes a revenue-sharing model and advisor control over client fee structure.
The page does not disclose individual compensation contracts or expense deduction ordering.

title: Savvy Advisors Form CRS, March 2026
publisher: Savvy Advisors, Inc.; hosted by SEC IAPD
claims: Client investment-management fees are negotiated, generally 0.3% to 1.9% annually.
Billing frequency, advance/arrears timing and valuation basis depend on client agreement.
Client fee terms do not establish advisor revenue-share rates.

title: Savvy Advisors Form ADV Part 2A, March 31, 2026
claims: Discloses household aggregation and prior-period-ending or average-daily asset valuation bases.
Describes prorating account starts/terminations and return of unearned advance fees.
Individual investment-management agreements remain the source for specific fee policies.

title: Technology platform for financial advisors
claims: Public workflows include advisor dashboard, household reporting, CRM, client portal and service tasks.
Savvy describes multi-custodian architecture above the custody layer.

title: The five principles that guide design at Savvy
claims: Public design guidance favors complete service workflows, clear ownership, role-specific attention and contextual learning.
The article describes neutral blue charts to avoid green implying positive financial performance.

title: Savvy: World Builders
claims: The article describes governed internal tools and server-resolved identity for user-specific analytics.
It is architecture context, not access to or verification of the earnings product.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Remote LATAM
claims: Advertised stack preferences include Rails, TypeScript, Next.js/React, SQL, GraphQL and automated testing.
Text was retrieved in search; direct open returned a JavaScript shell. This does not verify the current target codebase.

title: Terms and disclosures
claims: The technology parent and investment adviser are distinct entities.
Some advisor practice trade names are marketing identities rather than separate registered entities.

title: Core accounting
claims: Campfire describes multi-entity/multi-currency accounting, permissions, audit trails, reporting and source drill-down.
Product capabilities do not establish Savvy's installed configuration.

title: Revenue automation
claims: Campfire describes contract-based revenue schedules across subscription, usage, milestone and transaction models.
Revenue contracts should not be presumed to be advisor compensation agreements.

title: Forecast, powered by Ember
claims: Forecast distinguishes posted actuals, subledger commitments and estimated remainder with explanations.
The page does not establish advisor-share calculation, Savvy adoption or a public Forecast API.

title: Official Campfire API documentation index
claims: Index covers accounting, company objects, AP, AR, cash, reconciliation, revenue and report APIs.
Publishes OpenAPI location https://api.meetcampfire.com/api/schema?format=json; schema bytes were not retrieved in this research.

title: API quickstart
claims: API-key auth uses Authorization: Token; roles include admin, clerk and view only.
Published limit is 10 requests/second per API user; 429 supplies Retry-After.

title: OAuth apps
claims: Scoped OAuth access is intersected with authorizing-user permissions and selected workspace.
Access tokens last one hour, refresh tokens are documented at 30 days, and rate limits are per connection.
Feature availability may require workspace enablement.

title: Accounts payable workflows
claims: Bills relate to vendors, entities, expense accounts and optional departments/custom dimensions.
Guide documents create/pay/void workflows, which are outside the read-only prototype scope.

title: Accounts receivable workflows
claims: Invoices relate to customers, entities, products and optional contracts.
Guide shows separate invoice, service-period and payment concepts.

title: Creating journal entries
claims: Journal transactions include account/entity/currency and debit/credit representations with optional dimensions.
Journal-writing functions are not part of the offline reader.

title: List chart transactions
claims: GET /coa/api/transaction supplies GL lines with date/dimension and modification-time filtering.
include_deleted=true returns only deleted records; active and deleted streams are separate.
Pagination uses limit/offset; documented default history starts six months ago.

title: List journal entries
claims: GET /coa/api/journal_entry is the documented journal list path.
Journal data must not be added to its corresponding invoice/bill as a second economic event.

title: List invoices
claims: GET /coa/api/v1/invoice supports limit/offset and client, contract, entity, date and line-tag filters.
download=true triggers an async export and email; a read-only adapter must omit it.

title: List invoice payments
claims: GET /coa/api/v1/invoice-payments exposes allocation IDs, invoice linkage, amount/currency, dates, type, source and void state.
Supports cursor and modification-time incremental sync with voids visible.
CREDIT_MEMO appears in the example; a full payment-type enum and CASH semantics were not verified.

title: List accounting bills
claims: GET /coa/api/v1/bill is the documented bill list path.
Its relationship to advisor payables depends on actual accounting configuration.

title: List bill payments
claims: GET /coa/api/v1/bill-payments exposes bill linkage, amount/currency, payment date, source/source_id, void and modification timestamps.
Supports cursor pagination and modification-time incremental filters; omitted void filtering includes both states.

title: List revenue contracts
claims: GET /rr/api/v1/contracts exposes revenue-contract records.
The source does not establish that Savvy advisor compensation agreements use these records.

title: List bank reconciliation reports
claims: GET /coa/api/v2/reconciliation lists reconciliation reports.
A report's existence alone does not prove a particular advisor payment settled.

title: Webhooks
claims: Admin-managed signed webhooks cover invoices, bills, journals, contracts and credit/debit memos.
Payment and paid topics can both fire; deliveries may duplicate or arrive out of order.
HMAC uses timestamp plus raw body; subscription UUID is not an event identifier.

title: AI integration with Model Context Protocol
claims: Documents hosted MCP endpoint https://api.meetcampfire.com/mcp.
Documented tools cover accounting/company data, reports, budgets, contracts and aging; no authenticated use was performed.

title: Campfire is the first ERP with an MCP store
claims: Campfire describes an MCP store inside Ember.
This direction of integration is distinct from an external assistant calling Campfire's hosted MCP server.
